facts.raw_span: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of painful vision loss and floaters in her left eye
no history of myopia, ocular trauma, or surgery
Visual acuity was 20/30–2 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye
intraocular pressure was 21 mm Hg OD and 17 mm Hg OS
a mild nuclear sclerotic cataract and no inflammation
rare anterior chamber cells, 1+ vitreous cells, choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery, and an overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid
no retinal breaks were identified
Laboratory studies (CBC, basic metabolic panel, HIV, T-spot, syphilis screen, and ANCA panel) were normal
MRI of the brain and orbits showed mild posterior scleral enhancement but no intraocular mass
Fluorescein angiography showed late leakage in the temporal periphery
fundus autofluorescence was normal
optical coherence tomography revealed shallow subretinal fluid and a posterior vitreous detachment

concepts.why: The patient presented with painful vision loss and floaters, and imaging studies showed mild posterior scleral enhancement and late leakage in the temporal periphery, consistent with posterior scleritis.
The patient had a retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid and no retinal breaks, consistent with a serous retinal detachment.
The patient had rare anterior chamber cells and vitreous cells, indicating intraocular inflammation consistent with uveitis.
The patient had a posterior vitreous detachment, which is a common finding in patients with retinal detachment.
The patient had choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery, which can be associated with posterior scleritis and uveitis.
The patient did not have any retinal breaks, which is an important finding in the evaluation of retinal detachment.
The patient presented with painful vision loss and had imaging studies showing mild posterior scleral enhancement, consistent with scleral inflammation.
The patient did not have any specific findings suggestive of macular disease, but it is an important consideration in the evaluation of retinal detachment.
